stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +1.5%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $108.78 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-07-31, 115 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-07-31, 115 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-23.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-26) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: AI Solved Math’s Most Famous Problem. Now Humans Are Struggling to Understand It
stories.excerpt: It will take mathematicians months to understand the “alien” 17-million-line solution an Anthropic researcher produced for the Riemann hypothesis.
stories.lead:
Mathematicians are struggling to decode a 17-million-line solution to their field’s most famous problem, published by an Anthropic researcher on Friday.

Levent Alpöge released a proof in the programming language Lean of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis, which he had created with Claude. While the conjecture, which describes how prime numbers are distributed, is widely assumed to be true, many mathematicians have tried and failed to definitively show this, and the problem has become something of a holy grail of number theory.

stories.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
stories.excerpt: X says every Grok output is screened, but state AGs say Grok is still making CSAM.
stories.lead:
On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children.

SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM).

What’s new alongside Claude Ship are the PR Steward and Claude Approvals agents, which are launching in beta today.

stories.title: Nvidia Is Powering Brain-Computer Interfaces Now
stories.excerpt: Brain-computer interface company Paradromics is using Nvidia’s computing hardware and software to process brain data.
stories.lead:
A Michigan woman named Mary has a chip in her brain roughly the size of a dime. Though she struggles to speak due to motor neuron disease, the implant allows her to express her thoughts through a synthesized voice on a computer.

Made by brain-computer interface company Paradromics, the implant is outwardly invisible, but the speech decoding requires a cart full of electronics. A year from now, however, that cart will be transformed into a small box that can sit on her wheelchair, thanks to technology from Nvidia. Eventually, those electronics will be so small they’ll fit in a phone, says Paradromics CEO and founder Matt Angle.

stories.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, board chair
stories.excerpt: Trump says he spoke to the board and that Huang "did nothing wrong."
stories.lead:
“We’ve done a very thorough investigation and the investigation showed that… he had bad judgement having to do with somewhat unrelated incidents,” Trump said. “You have to protect our geniuses and there aren’t enough of them.”

Huang’s tenure at Nvidia dates back to the company’s founding in 1993, when he and three cofounders were focused on the then-nascent field of GPU hardware aimed at PC gamers. In the decades since, the highly parallel cores in those GPUs have been embraced first by cryptocurrency miners and then AI companies, propelling the company to its position as the most valuable in the world at its October peak.

stories.title: What should it cost to insure a home in wildfire country?
stories.excerpt: Some California homeowners have spent thousands making their homes safer from wildfires. Yet all that work has barely made a dent in their insurance bills. Should they be getting a bigger break?
stories.lead: As a homeowner in rural Northern California, I've lost a lot of sleep worrying about fires. It's not just that big, destructive ones are becoming more common. It's that finding affordable and reliable home insurance has become a nightmare. Without it, the most valuable asset I own could literally go up in smoke. And we've been stuck in a broken insurance market, hoping someone or something can fix it.

stories.title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
stories.excerpt: German media said Russia planned to launch a satellite with a nuclear warhead into space in coming weeks.
stories.lead:
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after German reports that Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.

Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media. It was not clear which country had authored the reports.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said such reports were "not new, yet they remain no less shocking", and a government spokesman said the reports were being taken "very seriously".

stories.title: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
stories.excerpt: Nvidia had come under pressure from President Trump to reappoint Huang, whose comeback helped add $1tn to the company's stock value.
stories.lead:
Jensen Huang has been reinstated as the boss of Nvidia less than two weeks after he was forced to resign following the revelations of extra marital affairs, one of which was with a suspected Chinese spy.

The AI chipmaker handed its co-founder his job back, despite rejecting his initial offer to return, after pressure from US President Donald Trump.

Trump said he "made the deal" with the tech giant's board to get Huang his job back, but both the president and Nvidia are facing backlash from lawmakers.

stories.title: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
stories.excerpt: Investigators say companies with ties to Donald Trump Jr's investment firm, 1789 Capital, have profited since his father's reelection.
stories.lead:
Congressional Democrats, led by likely House Judiciary Committee Chair Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, are expanding their investigation into the investment firm 1789 Capital, which brought on Donald Trump Jr. as a partner days after his father's reelection to the White House.

Since then, investigators say the firm has grown from "a middling venture capital firm" with $150 million in managed assets to "the darling of the venture capital world" with $3 billion in managed assets.

stories.title: For workplace culture champions, Jensen Huang's return is 'unfathomable'
stories.excerpt: Some who have worked to promote diversity and inclusion in Silicon Valley say Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO sends a message that all that matters is money.
stories.lead:
On Monday morning, a couple hours after Nvidia's board announced it had reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO, President Trump shared an AI-generated image on social media.

It's based on that striking photo of the president from 2024, just after he survived an assasination attempt. Surrounded by Secret Service agents, his face bloodied, Trump hoists a defiant fist in the air.

In the doctored photo, instead of Trump, it's Huang. An Nvidia flag flies behind him. And in his hoisted fist, he holds a red bra.

stories.title: They attended Trump's meme coin dinner. It didn't go well
stories.excerpt: Trump's meme coin dinners have sparked intense controversy. These two guests attended his latest on Sunday — and agreed to provide NPR inside access.
stories.lead:
Courtesy of Morten Christensen and Gabriëlle Felen/Morten Christensen

Headed to what some have called "the most exclusive dinner in the world," hosted by President Trump, crypto investor Morten Christensen and his young sister Gabriëlle Felen had butterflies in their stomachs.

The dinner on Sunday, Nov. 22, was meant to reward the top holders of the president's meme coin — a type of crypto currency that Trump had launched just days before his inauguration.

stories.title: Water Polo to Face Princeton in First Round of NCAA Championship
stories.excerpt: Fordham water polo to play Princeton in first round of NCAA Championship.
stories.lead:
Bronx, N.Y. - After winning its sixth straight Mid-Atlantic Water Polo Conference (MAWPC) title on Sunday, the Fordham water polo squad learned today that it will face off against a familiar foe in the first round of the NCAA Championship as the Rams will battle the Princeton University Tigers at the University of California at San Diego's Canyonview Pool in La Jolla, California, on Friday, December 4, at 5:00 p.m. (ET).

The Rams swept the two regular season matches with Princeton, winning 16-14 in the Bronx on October 10, and, 12-6, at Princeton on October 30.
